rationale: Consolidates recall of anatomical site–specific URTI pathogens established in the overview table that maps each site to its key bacterial, viral and fungal agents.
Tests understanding of the mechanism linking GAS pharyngitis to rheumatic fever via molecular mimicry — the key virulence concept established in this block.
Tests application of the correct confirmatory test for diphtheria toxigenicity after Albert stain identification — correlating stain morphology with the appropriate next investigation.
Tests application of laboratory diagnosis for EBV infectious mononucleosis — correlating the clinical triad and peripheral smear findings with the correct rapid confirmatory test.
Tests recall of the characteristic hyphal morphology of Mucor — a frequent point of confusion with Aspergillus; placed after the block covering fungal and parasitic URTIs including mucormycosis.
Tests recall of the correct procedural sequence for throat swab collection — a core practical skill for MI7.4; placed after the specimen collection and processing block.
Tests rapid recall of the age- and setting-specific LRTI pathogens tabulated in this block — the core MI7.3 competency of enlisting aetiological agents by clinical situation.
Tests application of laboratory identification methods for S. pneumoniae — the commonest CAP pathogen — correlating Gram-stain morphology with the correct confirmatory bench tests.
Tests understanding of why beta-lactams fail against Mycoplasma — a common prescribing error relevant to the atypical pneumonia triad established in this clinical pearl.
Tests application of current NI-KSHAY guidelines for managing an AFB smear-positive patient — linking sputum microscopy to the mandatory molecular confirmation step.

Tests application of treatment for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in an immunocompromised host — correlating GMS stain findings with the correct first-line drug; placed after the block covering viral and fungal LRTIs.
Tests the ability to match sputum microscopy stain appearances with the correct causative organism — the core MI7.5 practical skill of identifying LRTI agents on stained smears.
